taste.name: One condensed face for everything
taste.trigger: When choosing type for a portfolio that mixes a 216px name, poster headings and long artist statements
taste.decision: Chose Big Shoulders Display alone, in 2 weights (400, 600), over a display face paired with a separate body face
taste.reason: Condensed uppercase reads like exhibition wall lettering, so the whole site sounds like one curator's voice instead of a template
evidence: 137 of 137 sampled text elements use Big Shoulders Display
only weights 400 and 600 used, though 300-700 are loaded
nav, h1-h3 and body all from the same family

taste.name: The wall stays black so the art supplies the colour
taste.trigger: When deciding how much brand colour to put around saturated floral photographs
taste.decision: Chose a near-black #090909 field with white text and a single gold accent used once, over a coloured brand palette, cards or tinted panels
taste.reason: In a gallery the wall recedes; the reds of Brutiful and the blues of Kind of Blue stay the only chroma on screen
evidence: gold #C39C5D appears on 1 text element (the signature)
secondary text is white at 60% opacity rather than a grey hue

taste.name: Poster scale, then quiet reading
taste.trigger: When building hierarchy between headings and text
taste.decision: Chose extreme jumps (216px and 144px display against 20-24px text, about 7:1) over a gradual modular scale with mid-size headings
taste.reason: Each section opens like a poster title, then drops to a calm reading size, so the visitor always knows where a new room begins

taste.name: One work at a time, slow procession
taste.trigger: When listing the four series on the home page
taste.decision: Chose a single centred column of portrait thumbnails separated by 150px section padding and scroll reveals, over a 2-4 column card grid
taste.reason: Seeing one series at a time mimics walking past framed works; a grid would turn the art into products to compare
evidence: 0 CSS grids on the home page
thumbnails 3:4 at ~310px wide (21% of a 1440px viewport)
image reveal and scale-on-scroll animations on each thumbnail
